title: ACR MCP context_for_task Request v1
description: Ergonomic goal-only-by-default input for the context_for_task MCP tool. Only goal is required; repository, scope, budget, and requested_categories are optional overrides. There is no caller-supplied schema_version wire field: tool identity is established by the MCP call itself, not a wire field, matching the source_evidence request contract. scope.as_of pins retrieval to a point in time; scope.include_changed_files is a tri-state opt-in (omitted: sidecar default; true: include bounded git-changed files when scope.files is not explicitly set; false: never auto-include them) that lets a caller distinguish 'not specified' from an explicit choice. The sidecar maps omitted fields to fixed safe defaults before calling the hosted HTTP contract. On a hosted server there is no workspace to detect: repository.slug is required, MCP roots, the working directory, Git and the local index are never consulted, and scope.include_changed_files=true without scope.files is refused; pass repository and, if wanted, scope.files.

repository.description: The repository the task is about. On a hosted server it is required: the server cannot see your workspace, so omitting it returns a validation error that names repository.slug. On a local server it is optional and detected from the open workspace when omitted.

files.description: Repository-relative paths the task touches (up to 200, no duplicates). When set, these replace the automatic changed-files detection. On a hosted server this is how you supply changed files.

include_changed_files.description: Whether to add the workspace's git-changed files to the scope. Omitted: sidecar default. true: include a bounded list of changed files when files is not set. false: never add them. Not available on a hosted server unless files is set: true without files returns a validation error; list the paths in files instead.
